🇲🇽🚔 <u>Mexico City: High-Impact Crime Down 19% Under Brugada</u>

Security Secretary Pablo Vázquez told the Mexico City Congress that high-impact crime has fallen 19% under Clara Brugada. Homicides are down more than 18%, and the August and September 2026 levels "had not been seen in the last 20 years." Violent car theft is down 55%, and microbus passenger robberies are down 50%. Homicide convictions rose 18%, and police effectiveness reached a record 49.5% in public perception.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE: 37% Fewer Blackouts, Power Back in 7 Hours Instead of 25</u>

From January to September 2026, power interruptions fell 37% compared with 2024, CFE director Emilia Calleja reported. Average restoration time dropped 72%, from 25 hours in 2025 to 7 hours in 2026. She credited new infrastructure in Querétaro, Baja California, Yucatán, San Luis Potosí, Guanajuato, Tabasco and Sinaloa. Work has also started on the Playacar–Chankanaab II undersea line to Cozumel. CFE reported accumulated revenues of 332.2 billion pesos through the second quarter.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>Mexico City Moves to Cap Rent Hikes at Inflation</u>

Clara Brugada presented the Law of Tenant Relations and Fair Rents. Under it, rents in Mexico City could not rise faster than annual inflation, but they would not be frozen either. The bill also requires one-year minimum contracts in a digital registry and penalties for illegal increases. Tenants would provide a single guarantee instead of multiple co-signers, and a tenant ombudsman would give free legal defense. For the first time, the law recognizes gentrification as a process of social exclusion. About 30% of Mexico City families rent, and rents in the central boroughs have quintupled in 20 years.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Fake Government Websites Could Now Mean Prison</u>

Mexico's Chamber of Deputies voted 281 to 83 to reform the Federal Penal Code and the Industrial Property Law. Using, copying or imitating official government logos and symbols to commit fraud can now carry up to five years in prison. The target is criminal groups that build fake web pages dressed in government branding to charge people for procedures and payments. PRI, PAN and MC voted against and branded the bill the "Ley Antimemes", warning it could reach satire. The reform now goes to the Executive for publication in the DOF.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>980,000 Deported Under Trump, 400,000 of Them Mexican</u>

The Trump administration deported more than 980,000 people between January 20, 2025 and July 31, 2026, according to the Migration Policy Institute, as reported by La Jornada. About 400,000 were Mexicans. Only 20% of those deported had a criminal conviction. 69% were caught at the border, and interior arrests are up 151%. Of the people ICE removed, 61% had lived in the US for at least two years, and 15% for a decade or more.

🇲🇽🏭 "There was an economy secretary who went so far as to say the best industrial policy was the one that didn't exist. But we do have an industrial development policy for the country." "It has to do with substituting imports, strengthening the domestic market, creating new companies, and also the export economy. So there is a policy, and it is called Plan México." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 22, 2026 The private industrial parks association AMPIP presented 20 new parks in 8 states: 4.6 million square meters, room for 175 companies, 32,127 jobs and $763 million in investment. That makes 40 of the 100 parks promised under Plan México. INEGI's early estimate puts the economy 3.7% larger in September 2026 than a year earlier. The day before, 30 governors, Mexico City's head of government and about 500 mayors met with her to speed up permits for public housing and private investment.

🚨🇲🇽 "What is this of being a senator of the Republic and going around asking for foreign intervention?" "It turns out those two lives that were lost were foreign agents who had no permission for that operation, and it is also learned afterwards that they were carrying weapons." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 22, 2026 A reporter cited a May 20 interview in which Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos said state security officials met in Ciudad Juárez with US agents from the State Department, Homeland Security and the FBI. Sheinbaum recalled the operation: a pre-dawn drive at high speed on winding sierra roads to visit a meth lab that the agents had no authority to dismantle. Two of them died. A judge has since issued an arrest warrant in the case. Whether a crime was committed is for the Attorney General's Office to decide. "The governor's statements speak for themselves."

🇲🇽🌎 "There can be economic integration with sovereignty. There are some who think economic integration means ceding sovereignty, and we are not willing to do that." "We are not looking for conflict with the United States. What we are looking for is the best possible negotiation, for them and for us, without ceding sovereignty or territorial integrity." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 22, 2026 Revista Fortuna asked about a US "trilemma": bring production home, cut dependence on China, and stay competitive with Asia. Sheinbaum said a product can cross the border up to 16 times before it is finished, so jobs in Mexico also create jobs in the US and Canada, and North America competes better as a region. She cited Article 39 of the Constitution: sovereignty resides in the people. With the US in an election campaign, Mexico won't answer everything or fall for provocations.
